h1: Plearn Resort — a small stay near Erawan Falls that works well as a Si Sawat base
intro: Si Sawat is the district most people think of when they plan a trip to Erawan Falls or a raft house on Srinakarin Dam, but when it comes to finding somewhere to spend the night — a quiet air-conditioned room near the falls entrance — there aren't many small, affordable resorts to choose from. Plearn Resort is a small resort of about 7 rooms in Tha Kradan, Si Sawat, where every room is a Superior with air conditioning, breakfast is included, and there's free parking and free Wi-Fi. · What makes many people pick it is the location — only about 2 kilometres from Erawan National Park and Erawan Falls, and about 6 kilometres from Srinakarin Dam · Prices start at around THB 1,400/night · It's a small stay that still doesn't have many reviews, so this article walks through both the good points and the things to watch, based on the genuine reviews we could find, to make your decision easier before you book.

body.html: Who Plearn Resort is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Plearn Resort is a stay for people who have come specifically to visit Erawan Falls and the Si Sawat side of Kanchanaburi and want a quiet, clean air-conditioned room at a low price, without having to drive all the way back into Kanchanaburi town every night · It's not a luxury raft house floating in the middle of the dam selling waterfront glamour, and it's not a big resort with a pool or a spa · It's a small, family-run resort of about 7 rooms whose main selling point is being close to the Erawan National Park entrance and easy on the wallet · The genuine reviews we could find agree that the people best suited to it are families and groups of friends who drive in for an overnight trip to Erawan Falls, couples who want a simple bed close to nature, and budget travellers who value location and value for money over fancy amenities · On the other hand, if you expect a hotel with a pool, gym, lift, or full in-town hotel service, this may not be the answer, and you'd be better off considering a bigger resort or a pricier raft house instead · Overall, Plearn Resort plays on the words "close and good value" rather than on luxury, and that's the expectation to set from the start before you decide to book.

Location and getting there — this is unquestionably Plearn Resort's number-one selling point · The resort sits at 388/1-2 Moo 4, Tha Kradan, Si Sawat, Kanchanaburi, right on the main route to Erawan Falls · The highlight is that it's only about 2 kilometres from Erawan National Park and Erawan Falls — a few minutes' drive to the entrance gate — so you can get up early and join the queue up the falls ahead of the big crowds driving in from town · It's also about 6 kilometres from Srinakarin Dam, an easy onward trip to the raft launches or dam viewpoints · Slightly farther afield, the Hellfire Pass Museum is about 21 kilometres away, and if you want to head back into Kanchanaburi town — where the Bridge over the River Kwai and more restaurants are — allow about one to one and a half hours of driving depending on road conditions · An important note is that Si Sawat is a district with very little public transport, so having your own car or a rental you drive in yourself is almost essential, because hailing a taxi or hired car in the area is hard and expensive · If you don't have a car, plan your transport carefully before you set off, or ask the resort about a pick-up service in advance.

"We chose to stay here because it's so close to the Erawan Falls entrance — get up early, drive a few minutes, and you're there, up the falls before the crowds · The room is simple but clean, the owner looks after the place personally and is friendly, and the price is great value for a location like this."

Room types and decor — Plearn Resort is a small resort with about 7 rooms in total, and every room is the same type: a Superior Room, so you don't have to think much about which room grade to pick · The rooms are decorated in the simple style of an upcountry resort, focused on cleanliness and practicality rather than flashy design · According to the property's information, the rooms include air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, a large bed, an en-suite bathroom with toiletries, and a clothes rail · Several of the reviews we could find agree that the rooms are cleaner than expected for this price and the beds are comfortable, which is the most important thing for a stay of this type · Because it's a small owner-run resort, the atmosphere feels warm and friendly rather than like a large hotel system · One thing to know is that the rooms here are simple — they don't have luxury amenities like an electric kettle in every room or a full minibar the way in-town hotels do — so if you have personal items you rely on or want hot water to make your own coffee, bring them along just in case · Another thing to understand is that, being a small resort, rooms tend to fill up very fast on long weekends and during festivals because there are only a few of them, so if you're planning a peak-season trip, book several weeks ahead · Overall, Plearn Resort's rooms do a good job of letting you rest after a full day at the falls, at a price where a clean air-conditioned room near Erawan is harder to find.

Facilities and common areas — let's be straight from the start: Plearn Resort has no swimming pool, which is normal for a small resort in this area, so if you're after a pool for the kids to splash in, this isn't the answer — but the good news is that Erawan Falls, only about 2 kilometres away, has clear pools you can swim in all day in a way no swimming pool can match · The facilities that do exist, according to the property's information, are a dining room in the resort, a garden, a terrace to sit and relax, room service, free private parking, and free Wi-Fi in all rooms, along with the flexible welcome of a small owner-run resort · A point many people like is the garden corner and seating area, where it's quiet and peaceful — a nice spot to sip a coffee in the morning before heading out to the falls, or to relax after getting back · Free parking is a real advantage for people who drive in themselves, since almost everyone who comes to Si Sawat needs a car · As for Wi-Fi and phone signal in this area, you have to understand it's right next to a national park and mountains, so the signal may not be as strong as in town — if you need to work online during your trip, set your expectations accordingly · Overall, the facilities here are at a "just right for an overnight stay to explore nature" level: not focused on luxury, but enough for a comfortable stay on a budget.

Food and dining — Plearn Resort has a dining room serving an Asian breakfast that's already included in the room price, which is handy for anyone who wants a simple morning meal before heading out to the falls without driving around to find somewhere · Breakfast at a small resort like this is usually freshly made — rice porridge, eggs, coffee, home-style rather than a big buffet — which many people actually prefer because it feels warm, like eating at home · For other meals, since Si Sawat is a small district, the restaurants around aren't as dense as in town, but there are still some eateries and coffee shops in the area, such as those near Erawan Market and along the roadside, a short drive away · Some reviews suggest that if you arrive in the evening, plan your dinner in advance, because many local places close early · A common approach for families is to buy ingredients or food from Erawan Market and prepare it themselves, or to ask the resort about ordering dinner in advance · In short, food isn't the reason to come to Plearn Resort and eat in the resort, but the included breakfast and the convenience of not having to drive far in the morning are a nice fit with a waterfall-trip itinerary.

Service — service is another point that earns praise in the genuine reviews we could find · Because it's a small resort run by the owner and their team, the service leans friendly and flexible rather than like a big hotel system where everything follows a procedure · Many people say the owner gives good advice on routes to the falls, places to visit, and local restaurants, and helps with check-in and check-out as needed · There's a welcome service and room service as the property states · But to be straight, you have to understand that a small resort like this has a limited team, so at busy times when several rooms are checking in at once, the response may not be as quick as a hotel with lots of staff, and some things may have to be sorted out directly by phone or Line rather than at a front desk staffed 24 hours like an in-town hotel · People who like privacy and friendly, personal care will feel at home with this style, while those who expect big-chain hotel service should adjust their expectations first.

What real reviews say (both praise and criticism) — we have to tell it as it is: Plearn Resort is a small stay that still doesn't have many reviews across the various platforms compared with in-town hotels, so the picture comes from a small number of reviews that nonetheless point fairly consistently in the same direction · On the praise side: the thing mentioned most is the location so close to Erawan Falls, letting you get up early and go before the crowds; the value for money of getting a clean air-conditioned room on a budget; clean rooms and comfortable beds; a friendly, attentive owner and team; and a quiet, peaceful atmosphere good for resting near nature · On platforms like TripAdvisor and Trip.com, the scores for location, cleanliness, and value come out good to very good, even if they're from a small number of reviews · On the watch-out side: things to know are that there's no swimming pool and it's a small resort with simple facilities; getting there requires your own car because public transport in Si Sawat is sparse; the restaurants around are not dense and some close early; the Wi-Fi and phone signal may be weak because it's next to a national park and mountains; and because there are few rooms, it fills up fast on long weekends · Most of these caveats are things you can manage with advance planning and by setting your expectations to match the type of stay, rather than problems that put people off coming back.

"Clean room, not expensive, lovely owner who helped recommend places to visit · The only downsides are no pool and you need to drive yourself, because it's hard to hail a ride around here — but if you come to Erawan with a car, a location like this is really convenient."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Superior room is around THB 1,400/night including breakfast in the normal-price period, and it may climb a little on long weekends or during the waterfall season (roughly July to November, when Erawan Falls has plenty of water and looks lush and green) · Comparing it with other types of stay in the Si Sawat area makes the picture clearer: raft houses on Srinakarin Dam that are fancier and have water activities usually start at several thousand baht a night, and some are sold as packages including boat transfers, while bigger resorts with a pool also cost quite a bit more · So among land-based stays near the Erawan Falls entrance with clean air-conditioned rooms and breakfast included, Plearn Resort feels like good value within an affordable budget, especially for families or groups of friends who drive in themselves and plan to spend most of their time at the falls and the dam · What makes it genuinely worthwhile is the location, which saves both time and fuel because you don't have to drive in and out of town every day · If you measure value by "sleeping as close as possible to the attractions at a reasonable price," this place does it well — but if you measure by amenities per baht, a resort with a pool may feel like better value to some people.

What to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, you should have your own car or a rental you drive in yourself, because Si Sawat has little public transport and rides are hard to hail; a car lets you get around the falls, the dam, and to restaurants easily · Two, book several weeks ahead, especially on long weekends and during the waterfall high season, because with only about 7 rooms it fills up very fast · Three, set your expectations to match the type of stay — this is a small, simple resort with no pool, not a luxury hotel; if you're clear on that from the start, you'll be happy with what you get · Four, plan dinner in advance, because some local places close early; you might buy supplies from Erawan Market to prepare, or ask the resort about ordering food · Five, confirm your booking and check the details directly with the property — such as check-in time (generally from 2:00 PM), check-out before noon, pick-up service, and breakfast — through your booking channel or the resort's direct contact, for clarity since it's a small stay · Six, if you're set on Erawan Falls, check the park's opening hours and entry fee in advance and go early to avoid the big crowds.

Summary — based on the genuine reviews we could find and the property's information, Plearn Resort is the best fit for people who drive in for an overnight trip to Erawan Falls and the Si Sawat side of Kanchanaburi and want a clean air-conditioned room near the attractions at a budget price · The clear strengths are a location only about 2 kilometres from the Erawan Falls entrance, about 6 kilometres from Srinakarin Dam, an affordable price that includes breakfast, free parking, and the friendly care of a small resort · If you're looking for a stay with a pool, full big-chain hotel service, or arriving without your own car, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a raft house or a bigger resort at a higher price · But for a waterfall trip where you want the closest possible location on a comfortable budget, with a warm, friendly welcome — Plearn Resort answers that need well, in a way that isn't easy to find in this area · Just book early, because the rooms are few and fill up fast.

faq.q: Where is Plearn Resort · is it near Erawan Falls?
faq.a: The resort is at 388/1-2 Moo 4, Tha Kradan, Si Sawat, Kanchanaburi · It's only about 2 kilometres from Erawan National Park and Erawan Falls, a few minutes' drive away, and about 6 kilometres from Srinakarin Dam · It's a good base for exploring the falls and the dam on the Si Sawat side.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Plearn Resort · is breakfast included?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,400/night including breakfast for a Superior room in the normal-price period, and may climb a little on long weekends or during the high-water waterfall season · Prices can vary by platform and time of year, so compare and confirm with the property before booking.

faq.q: Does Plearn Resort have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool, because it's a small resort of about 7 rooms that keeps things simple · But the upside is that Erawan Falls, with clear pools you can swim in, is only about 2 kilometres away · If you want a pool at your stay, consider a bigger resort or a raft house instead.

faq.q: Who is Plearn Resort right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families, groups of friends, and couples who drive in for an overnight trip to Erawan Falls and Srinakarin Dam and want a clean air-conditioned room near the attractions at a budget price · If you're looking for a stay with a pool or full big-hotel service, or arriving without your own car, another type of stay may suit you better.

faq.q: How do I get to Plearn Resort · do I need a car?
faq.a: We recommend having your own car or a rental you drive in yourself, because Si Sawat district has little public transport and hired rides are hard to come by · From Kanchanaburi town it's about a 1–1.5 hour drive depending on road conditions · There's free private parking at the resort; if you don't have a car, ask the property about a pick-up service in advance.

faq.q: What restaurants and attractions are around Plearn Resort?
faq.a: The resort has a dining room serving breakfast included in the price · Around it there's Erawan Market and local restaurants a short drive away, but they're not dense and some close early, so plan dinner in advance · The main attractions are Erawan Falls (7 tiers), Srinakarin Dam, and the nature on the Si Sawat side · The Hellfire Pass Museum is about 21 kilometres away.
